# vergeio_vm_recipe_instance (Resource)

Deploys a VM from a catalog recipe, including a Windows recipe that uses cloudbase-init and a Linux recipe. Look the recipe up with [`vergeio_vm_recipes`](../data-sources/vm_recipes.md). `recipe_id` is that recipe's key.

`answers` is a map of question name to string. `vergeio_vm_recipes` lists each question's `name` and `type`.

A `disksize` answer is bytes. 50 GB is `53687091200`. `50` is fifty bytes. VergeOS would keep the image's own disk and still report success, so a value above zero and under 1 MB (1048576) is rejected before the request is sent. `0` keeps the recipe default.

A `bool` answer accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `1`, or `0`. Any other value, such as `enabled`, is rejected. VergeOS would store that value as false.

A `network` answer is a network name, a vnet key, or `__new_internal__`. `__new_internal__` is sent unchanged. A network name is resolved to its vnet key. Two networks with that name is an error.

The map is stored. It may contain a guest password. VergeOS does not return every answer, and the values it returns are coerced, so refresh does not overwrite `answers`.

Changing `name`, `recipe_id`, `answers`, or `auto_update` replaces the VM. Destroy sends one ACPI poweroff, waits `timeouts.delete` (default 2 minutes), kills the guest if it is still running, deletes the VM, then deletes the recipe instance.

This resource always deploys. It has no simulate argument.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "vergeio_catalogs" "operating_systems" {
  filter_name = "Operating Systems"
}

data "vergeio_vm_recipes" "windows" {
  catalog_id  = data.vergeio_catalogs.operating_systems.catalogs[0].id
  filter_name = "Windows Server"
}

# answers values are strings. A disksize question is bytes: 50 GB is
# 53687091200. 50 is fifty bytes and is rejected. A bool question accepts
# true, false, yes, no, on, off, 1, or 0. enabled is rejected.
resource "vergeio_vm_recipe_instance" "windows" {
  name      = "windows-01"
  recipe_id = data.vergeio_vm_recipes.windows.recipes[0].id

  answers = {
    HOSTNAME           = "windows-01"
    SELECT_CREATE_UEFI = "true"
    YB_DRIVE_OS_SIZE   = "53687091200"
    YB_NIC_ETH0        = "Internal"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import with the recipe instance key.

```shell
terraform import vergeio_vm_recipe_instance.windows <id>
```

`answers` is not read back. A configuration that sets `answers` on an imported instance plans a replacement.
